incident_and_fix.what_happened: An autonomous session (launched via `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` in a separate terminal) wrote all 200 posts' content and rendered 139 of them before being interrupted by the user, who noticed bullet text running off the edge of the canvas on multiple slides.
incident_and_fix.root_cause: scripts/compose_slides.py drew bullet_points with a plain draw.text() call and no word-wrapping (unlike headline/subheadline/body, which used the wrap-aware draw_multiline helper). Any bullet longer than ~8-9 words ran past the canvas edge. Audit found 773 bullets across 171 of 200 posts would have overflowed — Groups A/B (29 posts, written earlier with strict short bullets) were clean; Groups C-L (171 posts, written by the autonomous session with longer sentence-style bullets) were the ones affected.
incident_and_fix.fix_applied: compose_slides.py render_slide() now wraps bullet text with the existing wrap_text() helper, using dynamic per-bullet vertical spacing (extra line height added only when a bullet actually wraps, so already-correct single-line bullets keep their original spacing). Also added a console WARNING if wrapped bullet content would overlap the footer band.
incident_and_fix.verification: Re-rendered all 139 already-generated posts for $0.00 (cover images are cached separately from text compositing, so no re-billing was needed). All 695 slides re-passed QA. Zero footer-overlap warnings triggered.
incident_and_fix.status: RESOLVED — fix is in the shared renderer. All 200 posts (including the 139 rendered before the fix) were re-rendered under the corrected code and re-passed QA.
